title: Parliamentary Business Resources (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2017
short_title: Parliamentary Business Resources (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2017

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: This bill handles minor follow-up and switch-over issues from a new system for parliamentary work costs.
It removes the old rules for such costs, makes small updates to other laws, and sets up the transition to the new system.
The explanatory memorandum says the bill has no financial impact.
changes: It repeals the old parliamentary work expenses framework.
It makes minor consequential amendments to Commonwealth legislation.
It provides transitional provisions, including preserving the Parliamentary Injury Compensation Scheme Instrument 2016.
summary.affected: Members of Parliament and others who use parliamentary work expenses.

speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: The Parliamentary Business Resources (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2017 was moved for second reading, repealing the Parliamentary Entitlements Act 1990 and Parliamentary Allowances Act 1952 to implement a new principles-based expenses framework, with transitional provisions validating expenses spanning both systems and amending the Independent Parliamentary Expenses Authority Act 2017 accordingly.

speeches.speaker: Jim Chalmers
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Parliamentary Business Resources Bills, arguing they improve transparency and accountability for politicians' work expenses to help restore public trust, and noted that a previous independent review into parliamentary expenses—ordered after the former member for Mackellar used a helicopter on taxpayer funds—was delayed for over a year before action was taken.

speeches.speaker: Dan Tehan
speeches.brief: The Parliamentary Business Resources Bill 2017 and its consequential bill implement a key recommendation of the Tune-Conde review, establishing a new framework where parliamentarians can only claim expenses for the dominant purpose of parliamentary business, must ensure value for money, and face personal financial liability plus a 25% penalty loading for non-compliant expenses not repaid within 28 days.
